title: US Vice President J D Vance May Visit Pakistan For Iran Talks As Washington Explores Off-Ramp To Ongoing Conflict: Report
text:
World
Swarajya Staff
Mar 26, 2026 | Updated 09:23 AM GMT+5:30
Save & read from anywhere!

US Vice President JD Vance may travel to Pakistan this weekend for talks aimed at ending the month-long conflict with Iran.
The White House is working to arrange a meeting in Islamabad to discuss an off-ramp to the war, though the timing and location remain fluid.
Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif has positioned his country to host peace negotiations between Washington and Tehran.
Vance is reportedly being put forward as the probable chief negotiator from the US side if talks proceed.
Iran has expressed a clear preference for engaging with Vance rather than continuing discussions with Trump's special envoy Steve Witkoff or son-in-law Jared Kushner.
Iranian diplomatic sources view the vice president as a more acceptable interlocutor, citing his known scepticism of US involvement in Middle Eastern conflicts.
Tehran has refused to re-enter talks with Witkoff and Kushner following what it perceives as a breakdown in prior negotiations before coordinated US and Israeli strikes.
The US has shared a 15-point proposal with Iran through Pakistani mediators, addressing Tehran's nuclear programme, ballistic missiles, and maritime security in the Strait of Hormuz.
White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt insisted Vance has always been a key member of the president's national security team, though Iranian officials believe his participation could yield more productive results than previous negotiating teams.
The conflict, which began on 28 February, has seen missile and drone strikes across the region, with Iran essentially shuttering the Strait of Hormuz and sending global oil prices soaring.
